key_insight: Three neural models showed no statistically significant predictive differences after Holm correction but had complementary strengths in calibration and explanation reliability.
clinical_relevance: Reliable short-term glucose-risk forecasts could support proactive type 1 diabetes management, but clinical deployment requires further validation.
method: Built standardized prediction anchors from longitudinal glucose and multimodal patient data.
Compared Hybrid LSTM-Transformer, Multimodal Digital Twin, and State-Updating Digital Twin models under identical patient-level validation.
Predicted hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia at 30, 60, and 120 minutes while assessing calibration, explanations, disagreement, and robustness.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 5,503,441 anchors from 736 individuals in T1DiabetesGranada; the Multimodal Digital Twin had the lowest mean Brier score, and the State-Updating Digital Twin had the lowest mean ECE-10.
watch_item: Results from one dataset need external validation before generalizability and clinical readiness can be established.
paper_title: Reliability-Aware Short-Term Glycemic Risk Prediction Using an Anchor-Based Comparative Framework of Sequence, Multimodal, and State-Updating Digital-Twin Models
